title: Stock Market Live, Nov. 17:  Sensex, Nifty open higher after 10% November rally; global cues cap gains - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 17 November 2026

Indian equity markets opened mildly positive on Tuesday after the Nifty 50 and Sensex gained about 10 per cent in November, supported by record foreign portfolio investor inflows of $9.53 billion and resilient corporate earnings.

At 9.16 a.m., the Sensex was up 162.58 points, or 0.20 per cent, at 82,267.37, while the Nifty gained 48.75 points, or 0.19 per cent, to 25,339.85.

Overnight losses on Wall Street and weakness in Asian markets could weigh on sentiment, particularly after the US tightened efforts to restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.

Lower crude oil prices offer some support, but elevated US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and expectations of more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes may keep investors selective.

Ten stocks in focus: BSE, RRP Defence, ACME Solar, Dixon Technologies, Lemon Tree Hotels, SML Mahindra, P N Gadgil Jewellers, ARSS Infrastructure Projects, XTGlobal Infotech and B-Right Realestate are in the news following a series of business developments, including regulatory approval, strategic partnerships, project wins, acquisitions, fundraising plans and expansion initiatives.

“Crypto markets showed tentative signs of stabilisation, but the broader backdrop remains cautious. Bitcoin traded near $64,790, largely unchanged over 24 hours, while Ethereum edged up 0.48% to $1,822. Total crypto market capitalisation stood at $2.19 trillion, up 0.19%. However, the Fear and Greed Index remained at 13, indicating extreme fear and limited confidence in the recovery.

Global markets reflected a retreat from risk. The Nasdaq fell 2.49%, the S&P 500 declined 1.92%, and the Dow lost 1.41%. The VIX climbed 18.70% to 22.91, signalling increased demand for protection against volatility. The dollar index edged higher to 103.56, while gold also advanced. Together, these readings suggest a defensive investment environment that could constrain demand for crypto. Crypto flows also warrant attention. ETF outflows of $40.50 million were reported, while Bitcoin exchange balances increased by approximately 6,450 BTC to 2.59 million BTC.

Derivatives markets recorded $259.85 million in liquidations over 24 hours, comprising $135.42 million in longs and $124.42 million in shorts. The relatively balanced losses point to sharp moves in both directions.

Bitcoin open interest stood at $41.65 billion, up 0.35% over 24 hours, while its reported trading volume declined 2.20%. Between November 3–14, open interest fell from approximately $54 billion to $47 billion as Bitcoin declined, consistent with positions being reduced or liquidated. Ethereum open interest rose a stronger 3.76% to $22.42 billion, suggesting greater positioning activity despite its modest price gain.

For Futures traders, Bitcoin’s downside levels to watch are $64,000 and $63,000, while $65,000 and $66,000 are nearby resistance references. For Ethereum, support is around $1,800, followed by $1,750, with resistance at 1,850–1,900. Solana traders can monitor $70 and $68 on the downside, and $75 and $78 on the upside. XRP’s immediate support reference is $0.95, followed by $0.90, while $1.00 and $1.05 are potential upside hurdles.”

Top gainers of Nifty 50: Max Health (+2.67%), TMPV (+2.02%), BSE (+1.99%), Asian Paints (+1.86%), M&M (+1.38%)

Top losers: HCL Tech (-1.34%), ONGC (-0.85%), Tech Mahindra (-0.73%), Bharti Airtel (-0.72%), Infosys (-0.65%)

Vikram Subburaj, CEO, Giottus.com -- Bitcoin was trading around $64,600 on Tuesday morning, struggling to sustain a recovery after the weekend sell-off. The immediate resistance zone is 65,600-66,300, while support lies near $64,000 and $63,100. A sustained break below the latter could expose $62,300. Bitcoin remains well below its short-term holder cost basis of $75,600, leaving recent buyers under pressure. The market is also showing extreme fear, with CoinMarketCap’s Fear and Greed reading at 13.

Institutional demand remains weak. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $2.42 billion in net outflows between November 2 and 16. Stablecoin supply has contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days. However, much of the leveraged long positioning has been cleared, while some large-wallet cohorts have begun accumulating. These are tentative stabilisation signals, not evidence of a confirmed bottom.

The macro backdrop remains challenging. A Reuters poll of 101 economists found unanimous expectations of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, which would take the target range to 4.00%-4.25%. Investors will watch the November 18 release of the October FOMC minutes for further clues on the policy outlook. A stronger dollar and elevated bond yields could continue to constrain demand for risk assets.

Large-cap altcoins were mixed. Ethereum traded at $1,813.97, down 0.29%. BNB was at $590.66, down 0.10%, XRP at $0.9525, down 0.32%, and Solana at $71.71, up 0.28%. TRON was at $0.3041, down 0.87%.

Our advice: Avoid aggressive leverage and treat short-term rebounds cautiously. Consider staggered purchases, while watching ETF flows and Bitcoin’s ability to reclaim $66,300 for stronger evidence of stabilisation.

Purvang Mashru, Lead Analyst, BitDelta India

Bitcoin slipped 0.44% to about $64,536 over 24 hours, while Ethereum edged up 0.13% to $1,814. Major assets were mixed, with Solana gaining 0.31%, BNB down 0.36% and XRP lower by 0.60%.

The uneven moves suggest that the weekend recovery has not developed into a broad continuation.

Strategy bought 485 BTC during 9 to 15 November, 53.19% less than in the preceding week. Bitmine added 7,653 ETH in its 16 November update, down 20.17% from the weekly purchase reported on 9 November. These two buyers do not represent the whole corporate market.

Only $33.4 million of Strategy’s $244.7 million in net share-sale proceeds went to Bitcoin,
